subtitle: Executive Order 23-12 sets out councils, community advice, support for equity plans and reporting responsibilities. This plain-language course explains each one and connects it with the right source for your daily work.
scope: For DSD leaders, supervisors and staff who want to understand the signed order and its connection with agency work. This course does not establish new agency procedures or replace applicable law, policy, required analysis or authorized decisions. Learning can use practice cases, a suitable authorized draft or private reflection; no disclosure or live work product is required. Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.
introTranscript: Executive Order 23-12 continues two statewide councils and assigns responsibilities for collaboration, agency equity plans, community advice and reporting on a long-range plan. Understanding those responsibilities helps us avoid treating the order as either a symbolic statement or a detailed checklist for every staff task. The signed text describes specific statewide roles; related laws, DHS policies and agency plans provide other requirements. In these six lessons, we examine the order’s structure, connect plan actions with everyday questions, distinguish activity from evidence and practice identifying the responsible next step. The practice examples are learning situations, not descriptions of actual DSD performance. You can work at your own pace and reflect privately. Actual policy, reporting and accommodation duties remain in their applicable processes.

intro.heading: What the order actually says
intro.body:
Executive Order 23-12 continues the Governor’s One Minnesota Council on Diversity, Inclusion, and Equity and the Governor’s Community Council on Inclusion and Equity. The signed text gives them related but distinct roles. The One Minnesota Council brings agency leaders and equity practitioners together to collaborate on equitable practices and to monitor and advise on relevant legislative policies and state programs. The Community Council brings community advice into the collaboration and reviews the annual report.

The support offices also have distinct responsibilities. The Office of Inclusion facilitates and supports the One Minnesota Council and works with agency equity and inclusion practitioners on agency-specific equity plans and the long-range plan. The Governor’s Office of Equity, Opportunity, and Accessibility supports the Community Council. Those office names and assignments are what the signed text says; the course does not identify current officeholders or assign their responsibilities to a DSD supervisor.

The annual-report provision names the One Minnesota Council as responsible for preparing and presenting the report to the Governor. It starts in 2024 and sets December 31 as the submission date. The Community Council reviews it. That is a specific council obligation, not a statement that every unit must file this course’s worksheet by that date.

In a practice DSD meeting, Morgan is asked whether the order requires a particular credential in a posting or a tagged PDF export. Morgan should explain the councils and plan support, then identify the different source for the actual task requirement. A related requirement may be important without appearing in this order. The distinction avoids both dismissing the statewide direction and inventing steps the text does not contain. You can examine the practice question privately; a live work product is not necessary.

items.title: Collaboration and advice are meaningful roles
items.body: The councils do more than symbolize a value: the text identifies collaboration, monitoring, advice and reporting. At the same time, advice does not become automatic approval authority over every DSD decision. Morgan can explain the specific role rather than declaring that a council directs each unit’s hiring, document or service choice.

items.title: Support for plans is not a technical checklist
items.body: The Office of Inclusion’s agency-plan support connects statewide direction with agency work. The order does not list every step for a posting or bulletin. A staff question about those steps needs its applicable policy and process, with the connection to a plan explained where relevant.

items.title: Read the annual-report assignment precisely
items.body: The named council prepares and presents the report, and the Community Council reviews it. A unit may have an actual approved contribution process, but this course cannot invent one. Do not substitute a practice worksheet or unit deadline for the responsibility written in the order.

tabs.label: A statement of values only
tabs.body: This reading overlooks the text’s actual councils, support assignments and report provision. It can make staff think no responsibilities are named. Retain the equity purpose while explaining the concrete structure that supports collaboration and review.

tabs.label: A checklist for every task
tabs.body: This reading adds detailed requirements that the order does not prescribe, such as a particular hiring target or file-export step. A task requirement needs its own applicable source. Adding it to the order’s summary can confuse the responsible role and the evidence needed for a decision.

tabs.label: Specific statewide responsibilities
tabs.body: This reading names the councils, plan support and reporting, then distinguishes related task requirements. It lets Morgan answer the question without inventing authority or reducing the order to a slogan. Current agency procedures remain a separate source to check for actual work.

check.question: Which summary of Executive Order 23-12 is accurate?
check.correct: It continues two statewide councils, identifies plan support and collaboration/advice, and assigns council reporting and review responsibilities.
wrong: It requires every employee to pass a personal equity assessment.
It sets a numeric hiring target for every DSD unit.
It prescribes this course’s four preparation questions as the required analysis.
check.feedbackCorrect: The summary identifies what the signed text establishes without inventing a unit checklist.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The order does not prescribe a personal employee assessment, division hiring quota or this course’s preparation method. Those claims cannot be justified by attaching them to its equity purpose. Read the specific councils, support roles and report provision, and identify a different source when another duty applies.

A specific posting qualification must be justified through applicable employment requirements.

Choose a practice case for this course’s practice.

intro.heading: Connect statewide coordination with agency plans
intro.body:
The signed order describes a statewide setting for equity practitioners and agency leaders to collaborate on effective practices. It also identifies support for progress on agency-specific equity plans. This makes the relationship between statewide direction and agency work visible. It does not establish every DSD plan action, review schedule, current template or workgroup assignment. Those details must come from the actual approved plan and applicable agency process.

Imagine a practice unit whose proposed plan action is to improve how a provider notice communicates a service change. The unit schedules a discussion and identifies a draft notice for review. The discussion may help staff understand the issue, but attendance alone does not show whether the notice became usable or whether the intended recipients received the information they needed. Conversely, an unchanged sentence does not automatically prove failure; review may support retaining it with a reason.

Ask how the action connects with the intended improvement. What question is the unit examining? Which people and perspectives are relevant? What evidence would support the conclusion? Who has authority over the notice and its release? These questions help distinguish learning, planning, implementation and review without introducing a required routine that the order does not contain.

For a specific access question, identify the applicable source. Minnesota’s digital standard provides its own requirements, including WCAG 2.1 A/AA and Section 508 as qualified by that standard, within its scope and exceptions. A tagged file may be part of an improvement, but tags alone do not establish conformance. A proposed data breakdown may raise another question, but it cannot be assumed useful without defined measures, authority, quality and privacy protections.

These are practice possibilities, not claims about DSD’s normal practices or the prevalence of missed duties. Use them to understand how a plan can connect with everyday work. A real plan action still follows its actual responsibilities; this course does not create authority to change a posting, contract or notice unilaterally.

items.title: Activity can help without proving completion
items.body: The practice discussion could identify a concern or support a better review. It still needs a connection to the notice’s purpose and an honest account of what remains unknown. Do not discard a useful meeting simply because it is not the final result; do not use attendance as proof that every requirement has been met.

items.title: No change can have more than one explanation
items.body: A draft might remain unchanged because review supported the original choice, because the question was not examined or because an authorized next step is pending. The unchanged text alone does not tell you which. Ask for the actual review and reasons before assigning success, failure or motive.

items.title: Scope and authority make an action practical
items.body: An action about a notice needs the actual release roles and relevant requirements. A unit cannot infer permission to revise contract terms or job qualifications from the order’s equity purpose. Identify the question and use the responsible process for a proposed change, including any approval the actual work requires.

tabs.label: Report only the meeting
tabs.body: This account shows an activity but leaves the intended improvement unclear. A useful report can retain the meeting and add what question it addressed, what review occurred and what remains to be done. It should not claim a notice is accessible merely because the team discussed equity.

tabs.label: Assume unchanged means failure
tabs.body: This account treats the presence or absence of an edit as the entire outcome. A reasoned review might support an unchanged choice; an edit might also fail to address the relevant task. Examine the purpose, evidence and actual decision rather than using the number of changes as proof.

tabs.label: Connect action, purpose and evidence
tabs.body: This account distinguishes what the unit intended, what it did and what evidence supports its conclusion. It retains unknowns and actual authority. Staff can relate their work to the broader plan without pretending that the order prescribed their local method or that the activity completed every duty.

check.question: What can the practice unit conclude from scheduling a notice-review meeting?
check.correct: It has planned an activity; the intended improvement and actual requirements still need appropriate review and evidence.
wrong: The meeting alone proves every notice duty is complete.
An unchanged notice automatically means the team failed.
The order authorizes the unit to revise any related contract or posting immediately.
check.feedbackCorrect: The conclusion recognizes activity without making it an automatic outcome or authorization.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Attendance does not establish the notice’s usability or every requirement. An unchanged choice needs its actual reasons and review before judgment. The order’s support for plans also does not transfer unlimited change authority to a unit. Connect the activity with the intended question and responsible work process.

intro.heading: Interpret progress reporting and evidence carefully
intro.body:
Executive Order 23-12 directs the One Minnesota Council to prepare and present an annual report on the status and implementation of the long-range plan, beginning in 2024, with submission by December 31. The Community Council reviews the report. The text assigns those responsibilities to the councils. It does not prescribe this course’s practice note or create a reporting deadline for every DSD unit. An actual unit contribution must follow its real approved process.

To understand a progress account, distinguish several kinds of evidence. A meeting record can establish that a discussion occurred. A draft and review note can explain how a proposal was examined. Relevant implementation information can show what was put in place. Evidence about an outcome needs the measure, period, population and limits that support the conclusion. These distinctions help staff avoid treating activity as proof of a result or missing information as reassurance.

In a practice DSD data request, Dana is asked for a statewide count of a defined service event. The count may answer that overall question. A group comparison could answer a different question, but cannot be assumed informative from its labels alone. Dana would need appropriate authority, reliable definitions, data quality and privacy protections, including suitable treatment of small groups. Categories, missing information and overlapping populations can affect interpretation. This course does not direct a new collection or authorize disclosure.

Community perspectives also matter. A participant’s account can reveal a question that a count does not address, while an individual account cannot establish a population rate. The order’s community advice and review roles recognize a meaningful contribution; they do not make one council member the voice of every person or turn an advisory account into a complete statistical finding.

For learning, compare the claims in the practice request with the evidence each would need. A descriptive difference would not by itself show its cause. An absent complaint would not prove that everyone could use a process. Use a private or practice activity without collecting anyone’s personal information; real reporting and data work remain subject to their applicable authority and process.

items.title: Do not invent a unit deadline
items.body: The council report’s December 31 provision is specific. A unit might contribute through an actual agency process, but the order does not make the course’s practice note that process. Identify the real assignment rather than requiring learners to file a new report or declare their unit compliant from a worksheet.

items.title: Disaggregation is a question, not an automatic answer
items.body: A breakdown can be useful when the measure and comparison are valid and the work is authorized. It can also mislead if definitions differ, values are missing or privacy risks are unresolved. Dana should clarify purpose and feasibility, not promise that every breakdown reveals who is affected or why.

items.title: Community knowledge has its own value and scope
items.body: A person’s account may identify a practical barrier, a missing perspective or a question for review. Treat it respectfully without demanding that it stand for everyone. A statistical summary also does not replace the meaning of a particular experience; combine suitable evidence with its limits explicit.

tabs.label: One number answers every question
tabs.body: An overall count can answer a defined total question but cannot establish every subgroup experience or cause. Dana can provide the authorized supported figure and explain its scope. A further comparison needs a clear purpose and feasible, protected evidence rather than being assumed necessary for every request.

tabs.label: Every breakdown reveals the truth
tabs.body: More categories do not automatically create a valid explanation. Missing values, small groups, inconsistent definitions and authority can matter. A group difference also does not establish why it exists. Discuss what the proposed analysis could and could not show before presenting it as a finding.

tabs.label: Evidence matched to the claim
tabs.body: This approach identifies the question, supported measure, context and limits, then considers additional perspectives where relevant. It can preserve a useful overall count and a possible next inquiry. It does not substitute a practice unit note for the councils’ report or authorize new collection and disclosure.

check.question: Which interpretation of Dana’s practice statewide count is sound?
check.correct: The supported count can answer its defined overall question; a further comparison needs purpose, comparable data, authority and privacy, and cannot alone establish a cause.
wrong: The total proves every group has the same experience.
Any group breakdown automatically explains the cause of a difference.
The order authorizes collecting and publishing any new personal data needed.
check.feedbackCorrect: The interpretation matches the claim with the evidence and preserves actual data responsibilities.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A total does not establish every group’s experience. A descriptive difference does not explain its cause, and categories alone do not ensure comparability. The order also does not grant unlimited collection or disclosure authority. Clarify the question and use authorized, reliable and appropriately protected information.

items.text: The One Minnesota Council presents the annual report described in the signed text.
The Community Council reviews that annual report.
Are definitions and periods comparable for this proposed breakdown?
Can the analysis be performed with appropriate authority and privacy protection?
No complaints prove that everyone had meaningful access.
A rate difference alone establishes the cause of a disparity.

intro.heading: Use four optional preparation questions
intro.body:
The four questions in this lesson are an optional preparation method. They are not steps prescribed in Executive Order 23-12, and they are not a replacement for DHS’s required equity work. You can use them with a practice posting, notice or meeting proposal to make a question more specific before identifying the actual review process.

First, who is affected? Identify the people and roles relevant to the item without treating a whole group as identical or inventing their preferences. Second, what is unclear or missing? Name the question about participation, evidence or the decision that needs attention. A missing answer is a reason for inquiry, not proof of a violation or permission to speculate about intent. Third, which requirement applies? Locate the actual law, policy or approved process. Fourth, what next step is appropriate? Distinguish a proposed edit, an authorized action, a formal request and a question needing guidance.

The DHS Equity Policy has its own toolkit uses and formal-analysis procedure. For actions with prolonged or long-term impact scheduled for the approvals identified in the policy, the action must be accompanied by the relevant DHS Equity Analysis or Equity Scan, or a customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director for relevance to the business area. Other stated employee responsibilities also remain in place. A short preparation note cannot certify that these requirements are complete.

In a practice posting draft, Avery wonders whether a copied qualification reflects the job’s actual needs. The questions can clarify that issue and support an appropriate HR review. They do not authorize immediate removal of the requirement, prove the rule discriminatory or establish that an equivalent-experience option is required for every credential. Actual job requirements and posting authority still matter.

You may keep the exercise private and use an example. If an actual item is involved, use a suitable authorized draft without personal information and preserve its required review and approval. Learning does not require finding a defect, changing a sentence or producing a live record; a supported unchanged choice can be a valid conclusion of an actual review.

items.title: Preparation narrows the question
items.body: Avery can ask what skill the credential is intended to represent and which actual rules apply. That is more useful than assuming every copied requirement is invalid. The method gives a clear question to the person responsible; it cannot replace that person’s evidence or authorize a change.

items.title: A proposed edit differs from approval
items.body: Drafting a clearer sentence or an alternative qualification for review can be appropriate within the role. Posting it as an approved change is a different action. Use the actual HR, communications, procurement or other review process when it applies, rather than inferring approval from the order’s equity purpose.

items.title: Recognize required analysis without certifying it
items.body: The DHS policy names formal-analysis conditions and required tools. Identify whether and how the requirements apply through the actual process. This practice can help prepare relevant information, but a completed four-question note is not proof that the formal analysis or all policy responsibilities have been satisfied.

tabs.label: Change immediately because it seems useful
tabs.body: This approach skips the actual requirements and authority. A proposed qualification change can affect the job and selection process, so Avery must use the responsible review. A useful equity question is not permission to remove every requirement or bypass applicable approval.

tabs.label: Keep it because it was used before
tabs.body: This approach treats a past version as sufficient evidence for the present decision. The prior text may be supported, but the current question still deserves an appropriate review. Ask what the actual job needs and which rules apply without assuming either validity or discrimination from age alone.

tabs.label: Prepare and use the responsible review
tabs.body: This approach clarifies the affected people, open question, source and next step, then uses the actual process. It permits a proposed change or supported unchanged choice. It does not claim that the preparation is the order’s checklist or the required DHS analysis.

check.question: What should Avery do with the question about the practice posting’s copied qualification?

wrong: Remove the qualification immediately because equity always requires fewer credentials.

check.feedbackCorrect: The response uses preparation to inform the real review without creating authority or claiming policy completion.
check.feedbackIncorrect: Equity questions do not invalidate every credential or authorize unilateral changes. A prior posting does not settle the current job question. Four practice answers also do not replace the formal DHS analysis/scan or relevant customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director. Use the actual review and requirements.

intro.heading: Recognize concerns that require a formal response
intro.body:
A statewide equity framework can support understanding, but an actual concern may already require a specific response. Executive Order 23-12 does not replace those policies or assign every matter to a program consultant. Optional guidance can help staff learn or think through work; it is not a prerequisite for a required report, request or other formal action.

MMB Policy 1432 addresses general respectful-workplace concerns within its scope. Protected-class harassment and sexual harassment are excluded and addressed through the separate applicable policies. In a practice conversation, a staff member tells a supervisor that a coworker repeatedly mocks their religious dress. This is a protected-class concern for Policy 1436, not a matter to hold in an optional team discussion. Managers and supervisors must immediately report allegations or incidents of protected-class harassment or discrimination to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and comply with agency procedures. Employees and third parties are strongly encouraged to report; that differs from the manager’s mandatory duty.

The supervisor can listen, respond appropriately and explain that the report must follow the actual process. Do not require confrontation, mediation, a written account or consultant approval before the required manager report. Do not promise unlimited confidentiality or independently decide a finding or corrective action outside assigned procedures and authority. This preserves, rather than prohibits, any investigation or response actually assigned under agency procedures. Retaliation is prohibited.

Employment accommodation has another process. In a second practice exchange, a staff member asks for a usable meeting document because of a medical condition. Policy 1433 recognizes requests without special legal words. The recipient promptly forwards the request to the appropriate decision maker and tells the person who that is. Actual agency delegation determines the decision role. Supervisors and managers must not request medical information or documentation; the ADA Coordinator makes an appropriate documentation request, and agencies do not request or accept medical records as accommodation documentation.

Use these invented examples for learning without disclosing a colleague’s concern. A course cannot decide an actual complaint or accommodation, but it can help you recognize which responsibility must proceed independently of the optional exercise.

inThisLesson: Distinguish a protected-class concern under Policy 1436 from the general respectful-workplace scope of Policy 1432.
Identify a manager’s immediate HR or Affirmative Action Officer reporting duty and preserve assigned agency procedures.
Recognize an ordinary-language employment-accommodation request and identify the prompt forwarding and ADA Coordinator information roles.
What should the supervisor do?
lessons.keyStatement: Provide a respectful response and use the applicable process without delaying it for discussion or optional consultation.

flashcards.back: General respectful-workplace concerns; protected-class harassment and sexual harassment use the separate applicable policies.
Immediate report of protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer, with agency procedures followed.
A request for a change or assistance because of a medical condition can begin the accommodation process without a legal phrase.
Appropriate accommodation-documentation requests belong to the ADA Coordinator; supervisors/managers do not request medical information and medical records are not accepted documentation.

items.title: The person’s options and the manager’s duty differ
items.body: The staff member may choose an available reporting route and is not required by this course to confront the coworker. Once the supervisor receives the protected-class allegation, Policy 1436 requires the immediate HR or Affirmative Action Officer report. Explaining support options does not make that duty dependent on the person’s agreement to report.

items.title: Preserve assigned procedures and authority
items.body: Do not hold an improvised team investigation or decide discipline outside the actual role. That limit does not remove a manager’s assigned agency investigation or corrective-action responsibilities. Follow the actual complaint and investigation procedures, including authorized information handling, rather than creating a blanket prohibition or an informal substitute.

items.title: Recognize and forward without collecting medical detail
items.body: The employment request needs prompt forwarding, not a demanded diagnosis or special form before recognition. The recipient tells the person who the appropriate decision maker is. A shared-document improvement may also need work, but it does not erase the request or permit supervisor medical-information collection.

tabs.label: Treat the protected-class report as optional discussion
tabs.body: This approach can postpone the manager’s immediate reporting obligation or put pressure on the staff member to handle the issue personally. A learning conversation and support can be useful, but the protected-class allegation must proceed to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer under Policy 1436. Do not make consultant review a gate.

tabs.label: Resolve every request within the team
tabs.body: This approach may seem quick but can create unassigned decision or information roles. A manager does not gain authority to request accommodation medical documentation from the course, and does not independently decide a complaint outside agency procedures. Use the actual decision roles and preserve any properly assigned responsibilities.

tabs.label: Recognize the matter and use its process
tabs.body: This approach listens and responds respectfully while keeping the specific duty moving. Immediate protected-class reporting and prompt employment-request forwarding are different requirements, with distinct roles. It preserves support, actual authority and privacy without guaranteeing an outcome or requiring disclosure for the course.

check.question: In this example, a supervisor receives a report of repeated mockery of a staff member’s religious dress. What is required?
check.correct: Immediately report the protected-class allegation to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow agency procedures, while responding respectfully and avoiding retaliation or improvised action outside authority.
wrong: Wait for the staff member to decide whether the supervisor should report.
Require confrontation or mediation before using the policy process.
Treat the matter only as Policy 1432 respectful-workplace learning.
check.feedbackCorrect: Religion is a protected-class concern under Policy 1436. The manager’s reporting duty is not replaced by optional discussion or consultant guidance.
check.feedbackIncorrect: The staff member’s reporting choices do not cancel the supervisor’s immediate duty. Confrontation and mediation are not prerequisites to the required report. Policy 1432 excludes protected-class harassment; use Policy 1436 and actual agency procedures. Preserve properly assigned investigation responsibilities rather than conducting an improvised process.

items.text: A manager immediately reports protected-class allegations to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer.
Follow assigned agency complaint/investigation procedures and prohibit retaliation.
Promptly forward an ordinary-language request and identify the appropriate decision maker.
The ADA Coordinator makes an appropriate medical-documentation request.
A supervisor demands medical records before forwarding the request.
Consultant approval is required before the manager’s protected-class report.

scenario.context: DSD practice case: A staff member asks a supervisor for a usable meeting document because of a medical condition. The supervisor wants medical records first and plans to discuss the issue at a team learning meeting.
options: Request the full medical record and share it with the team.
Postpone recognition until the person uses a legal phrase.
Recognize the request, promptly forward it to the appropriate decision maker and tell the person who that is, leaving any appropriate documentation request to the ADA Coordinator.
responses: Medical records are not accepted accommodation documentation, and supervisor collection is prohibited.
Policy 1433 does not require special legal words for initial recognition.
This preserves the formal process and information roles without promising a particular accommodation.

lessons.transfer: Use either practice exchange to distinguish a required next step from optional support. No actual complaint or health information needs to be entered or shared.

move.control: You can recognize the applicable reporting or request process.
move.failure: A required response waits for learning, consultant approval or an improvised team decision.
move.next: Use the specific policy, responsible role and actual procedure without delay.

takeaways: A clear account identifies the source and the responsible role.
Practice can use an example or private reflection; a live work product is not a completion condition.

intro.heading: Practice the source distinctions and a next step
intro.body:
The final exercise brings the course’s distinctions together. Choose the practice provider-notice example, a suitable authorized draft without personal information or private reflection. Identify a responsibility actually named in Executive Order 23-12, a separate applicable requirement relevant to the task, and a question that the available evidence cannot yet answer. This is a learning choice, not a new work deadline or an assigned report.

In the practice example, Quinn’s unit has discussed a provider-notice draft and exported a tagged file. Quinn wants to describe this as proof that the order and all access requirements have been met. The course now gives a more precise explanation. The order establishes the councils and plan support; the notice has its own applicable requirements. A discussion and tags may show steps taken, but they do not establish every conformance criterion, effective communication or a council reporting obligation.

A useful practice note can say what question was examined, what evidence supports the current account and what remains to be checked through the actual process. If an appropriate review supports an unchanged choice, the note may explain that reason. Learning does not require discovering a defect or making an edit. A plain-language sentence, tagged export or absence of complaints is not automatically evidence that every person could use the notice.

For actual work, preserve the responsible review, approval and required analysis. A proposed change to a posting, notice or contract needs the relevant authority. An actual employment request or protected-class concern follows its specific process without waiting for the exercise. The short note also does not replace the annual report assigned to the One Minnesota Council or its review by the Community Council.

You can finish by privately explaining the distinction to yourself, or practice through Quinn’s example. A deeper understanding is worthwhile without a recorded reflection, colleague disclosure or live work record. If you choose a real next step later, make it within the actual role and agreed process rather than treating the course’s suggestion as a mandatory Friday or three-business-day schedule.

inThisLesson: Explain a named responsibility in the order and distinguish it from a task’s applicable requirements.
Use a practice work item or suitable authorized draft to identify evidence, limits and a responsible next step.
Distinguish an optional learning note from required analysis, reporting and actual decision authority.
Which account is supported?
lessons.keyStatement: Keep the source, evidence and next step clear without turning practice into a claim of compliance.

flashcards.back: An account that names the actual order responsibility and the separate source for a task requirement.
An optional learning account of a question, supporting evidence and unknowns; not a substitute for required analysis or reporting.
A conclusion retaining a choice after appropriate review with reasons; an edit is not always the necessary outcome.
An actual next step within the relevant authority and process, rather than a deadline invented by this course.

items.title: Explain the tagged-file example carefully
items.body: The tagged export may address a particular problem and still need other applicable checks. Quinn can describe the step without calling it complete conformance or proof of effective communication. The notice-review evidence and actual requirements determine the supported conclusion; the order is not the technical standard.

items.title: A note can preserve uncertainty
items.body: The practice note might record that the intended task or a requirement is still unclear. That is not an automatic failure or proof of harm. It identifies what appropriate review would need next. Do not fill the uncertainty with a reassuring result, a group assumption or a finding unsupported by the evidence.

items.title: Keep private learning legitimate
items.body: You can understand the council and source distinctions without producing a live notice or sharing a personal story. The exercise remains available through an example or private reflection. Actual duties still need action when they arise, but course completion is not a personnel assessment or certification that those duties were performed.

tabs.label: Plain and tagged means complete
tabs.body: This approach treats two potentially useful features as proof of every requirement. It may overlook other applicable criteria, the actual communication task or the limits of the evidence. Describe the steps and use the responsible review before claiming conformance or effectiveness.

tabs.label: No edit means no useful learning
tabs.body: This approach assumes that learning must produce a change or a live work record. A supported unchanged choice or a clearer question can also matter. Do not manufacture a defect or require private disclosure to create an output; preserve real duties separately from the learning exercise.

tabs.label: Supported account with a next question
tabs.body: This approach names the relevant source, what was examined and what remains unknown, then identifies the actual next process where needed. It can be practiced privately with Quinn’s practice notice. It does not certify the notice, replace required analysis or claim the council report is complete.

check.question: What can Quinn conclude from a discussion and tagged export of the practice notice?
check.correct: Those steps can be described with their purpose and limits; applicable review and evidence are still needed before claims of conformance, effectiveness or completion of required duties.
wrong: The order and every access requirement are automatically complete.
The note replaces the councils’ annual reporting responsibilities.
A useful exercise requires a live edit and public reflection from every learner.
check.feedbackCorrect: The conclusion preserves useful work without stretching it into certification, reporting or a compulsory learning output.
check.feedbackIncorrect: A discussion and export do not establish every requirement or outcome. A unit note is not the One Minnesota Council’s report or Community Council review. Learning can use an example or private reflection and can support an unchanged choice with reasons; it does not require disclosure or a live edit.

items.text: Use Quinn’s practice notice to explain a source distinction.
Reflect privately on what the order does and does not prescribe.
Use the required DHS analysis when the policy applies.
A real protected-class report or employment request follows its specific process.
Tags and a plain summary prove complete access for everyone.
A practice note fulfills the order’s council report provision.

lessons.next: Continue at your own pace: Use the job aid when a source distinction or next question would help

scenario.context: DSD practice case: Quinn wants to mark a plan action complete because the team discussed a notice and exported tagged text. No full applicable review or outcome evidence has been supplied.
options: State that every duty is complete because tags are present.
Describe the steps, identify the applicable source and remaining evidence, and use the actual review process before making a completion claim.
Require all learners to publish a live change this week to prove they learned.
responses: Tags alone do not establish every criterion or effective participation.
This retains the work performed and its limits without inventing a finished result.
The optional learning exercise is not a compulsory live-output deadline.

lessons.transfer: Use an example, private reflection or a suitable authorized draft to explain one source distinction and a next question. No disclosure, live edit or recorded output is required.

move.control: You can explain the order accurately and identify a task’s separate source and process.
move.failure: A short practice output becomes automatic compliance, a council report or a mandatory personal record.
move.next: Retain the actual responsibility and the evidence still needed for a real conclusion.

jobAid.subtitle: Read the responsibility, identify the source and use the actual process.
remember: EO 23-12 establishes statewide councils, collaboration, plan support and reporting/review responsibilities. It is not every unit’s technical checklist.
Identify the applicable law, policy or approved process for a particular task.
Activity, a tagged file or an edit count does not automatically establish implementation, access or an outcome.
Optional practice and private reflection do not replace actual required analysis, reporting or requests.

sections.heading: Keep the order’s structure clear
items: The One Minnesota Council collaborates, monitors/advises and prepares the annual report described in the order.
The Community Council advises and collaborates, and reviews that annual report.
The Office of Inclusion supports the One Minnesota Council and agency-specific equity-plan progress; the Governor’s Office of Equity, Opportunity, and Accessibility supports the Community Council.
The signed report provision starts in 2024 and names December 31. Do not turn it into an invented deadline for every unit’s practice note.

sections.heading: Use optional preparation questions
items: Who is affected, and what perspective or evidence is relevant?
What is unclear or missing, without assuming a cause or a violation?
Which actual requirement and decision role apply?
What next step fits the role’s authority and responsible process?
Use a practice example, private reflection or suitable authorized draft. A live edit, disclosure or recorded learning output is not required.

sections.heading: Preserve actual requirements and evidence
items: DHS Equity Policy’s required tools and formal-analysis procedure remain separate from the short exercise.
A customized tool under that procedure is developed in consultation with an equity director for relevance to the business area; the course note does not fulfill it.
A group comparison needs clear purpose, reliable comparable definitions, actual authority and appropriate privacy protection. A descriptive difference does not establish cause.
Tags and plain wording can be useful features without establishing all accessibility criteria or effective communication.
Input can support a changed or unchanged choice; explain how it informed the decision and retain unknowns.

sections.heading: Recognize the formal response
items: For protected-class allegations or incidents, managers/supervisors immediately report to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow assigned procedures under Policy 1436. Optional consultant guidance is not a reporting gate.
Policy 1432’s general respectful-workplace scope does not replace the separate protected-class or sexual-harassment policies.
For an ordinary-language employment accommodation request, promptly forward it to the appropriate decision maker and tell the person who that is.

Supervisors/managers do not request medical information or documentation. Appropriate accommodation-documentation requests belong to the ADA Coordinator; medical records are not accepted documentation.
Preserve authorized investigation and decision responsibilities. Do not improvise an investigation, disclosure or corrective action outside actual procedures and authority.
Native American- and Tribal-specific matters are referred to the appropriate office within ADSA.

sources.title: Executive Order 23-12: Official signed order
sources.note: The four-page signed text establishes the two councils, support offices, agency equity-plan connection and annual-report responsibilities. This course’s preparation questions are not a method prescribed in the order.

sources.title: DHS Equity Policy
sources.note: Agency equity responsibilities, specified toolkit uses and the formal-analysis procedure. A short practice record cannot replace the required toolkit analysis/scan or a relevant customized tool developed in consultation with an equity director.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1432: Respectful Workplace
sources.note: General respectful-workplace scope. Protected-class harassment and sexual harassment are excluded and addressed through the separate applicable policies.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1436: Harassment and Discrimination Prohibited
sources.note: Managers and supervisors immediately report protected-class allegations or incidents to HR or the agency Affirmative Action Officer and follow assigned agency procedures. Employees and third parties are strongly encouraged to report; retaliation is prohibited.

sources.title: MMB Policy 1433: ADA Reasonable Accommodation
sources.note: Ordinary-language requests, prompt forwarding, actual decision roles and ADA Coordinator documentation responsibilities. Supervisors/managers do not request medical information or documentation; medical records are not accepted as accommodation documentation.

sources.title: Minnesota State Accessibility Standard, version 4
sources.note: State digital standard effective July 1, 2024: WCAG 2.1 A/AA and Section 508 as qualified by the standard, within its scope and exceptions. Tags or a readability claim alone do not establish conformance.

sources.title: DOJ: Effective communication
sources.note: Task, context and individual communication methods matter to effective communication; public-entity primary consideration has its actual rule and limits. These duties do not originate in EO 23-12.
